name: @oscharko-dev/keiko-ui
description: Keiko Wave 1 local UI (static export). Build-time-only; served by the Node BFF in keiko-server.

scripts.typecheck:native: npm --prefix ../.. run check:typescript-toolchain && node ../../node_modules/@typescript/native/bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --incremental false

_browserslistRationale: Corrected from chrome/edge>=79, firefox>=72, safari>=13.1, which the shipped UI code has not
satisfied for a long time: Array.prototype.at(-n) appears 35 times across 22 production files
(Firefox 90, Safari 15.4), crypto.randomUUID 24 times across 13 (Firefox 95, Safari 15.4),
Object.hasOwn 9 times across 6 (Firefox 92), and lib/api.ts uses AbortSignal.timeout (Firefox
100, Safari 16) — every one beyond the old floor, so the declaration promised engines on which
the app cannot start. Counts are occurrences and files stated separately on purpose: the
gate's own messages report FILES, and conflating the two produced three wrong numbers here.
AbortSignal.any is feature-detected with a fallback in first-party lib/api.ts. The declared
floors are derived independently from the actual first-party and bundled-dependency closure;
they are not presented as one Baseline release set. check:browser-baseline enforces that closure.
CSS also contributes real floors: 32 :has() rules across 6 stylesheets
DEFINE custom properties that later declarations consume (absent, not merely unstyled, below 121),
and globals.css uses oklch() 190x and color-mix() 590x (Firefox 113) with no @supports fallback —
an engine that cannot parse a colour value drops the whole declaration, which for a theme built on
them means unreadable text, not a cosmetic shift. Declarations that DO degrade gracefully
(text-wrap: balance) are deliberately not gated: listing them would manufacture pressure to raise
a support floor for a nicety.
The bundled-dependency scan derives the full transitive browser graph from first-party value
imports and worker URLs, including Monaco's ESM main/worker closure and PDF.js. PDF.js uses its
legacy main AND worker entries: those retain newer call sites such as Promise.try and URL.parse
but execute bundled core-js implementations before them in each realm. The required browser
smoke deletes those host APIs and parses a real tiny PDF through a real worker, proving the
compatibility path rather than inferring it from a grep. Dependency calls that are not bundled
with a matching implementation still raise the declared floor. Monaco's reachable source uses
Intl.Segmenter, which sets Firefox 125; PDF.js's non-polyfilled AbortSignal.any sets Chrome/Edge
116 and Safari 17.4. WebKit is a required smoke proxy for Safari, not a claim that Playwright's
patched Linux WebKit build is byte-identical to Safari 17.4 on Apple platforms.
